title: Connection thermostat and slowpath trickle-shedder, plus canary hotfix
author: Nadia Thompson
description: Context: Recent incidents under regional slowpath spikes (SUP-9123) showed large bursts of open backend connections and a cascade of slowpath requests that pushed SLOs past the alert threshold. The canary deployed the initial admission gate but revealed oscillation (rapid open/close) when burst traffic subsided. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a Connection Thermostat layer that caps and smooths new outgoing connection ramp-ups per-region per-pool, with a PID-inspired dampener to avoid rapid reopen cycles; (2) a Slowpath Trickle-Shedder that converts abrupt slowpath admission into a tokenized trickle stream when queue depth and avg latency cross configured SLO markers. Both changes are guarded behind runtime flags and include an emergency rollback switch. Checklist: - implement thermostat algorithm and bounded queueing - implement trickle-shedder token allocator and backpressure hooks - add metrics (thermostat_setpoint, trickle_tokens_granted, slowpath_sat_rate) and traces for handoff paths - unit tests for edge windows, scheduler fairness, and stepdown - integration canary: 10% traffic region for 2h, telemetry gating - add documentation of config knobs and safety rollback Notes on design: Thermostat keeps a soft target for concurrently opening backend connections and slowly adjusts the target based on short-term latency and connection success rate. A short cooldown prevents immediate reopen after a hard clamp. Trickle-shedder uses a leaky-token approach: when slowpath load exceeds threshold, new slowpath admissions are scheduled into a paced stream (configurable burst+rate) instead of immediate admission; this flattens downstream KV and GPU load while preserving prioritized throughput for high-SLO tenants. Testing & rollout: Ran synthetic spike tests against perf-lab and a 6-hour canary in us-west-2 with traffic mirroring. Initial CI run hit a flaky test (scheduler/alloc_test.go) which was fixed by guarding timeouts; final CI passed. Rollout plan: enable runtime flag in main->canary 10% region->observe 24h->ramp to 100% with 1h pauses and alert thresholds. Revert plan: runtime flag off + immediate connection drain (fast-drain=false) and regional rollback script in runbooks. Related: ENG-1982 (SLO enforcement work), SRE-54 (incident follow-up).

review_comments: Ethan Martinez: Good idea to smooth connection ramps. Two asks: expose the thermostat setpoint as a tag and add an emergency disable in flags. Also, can you explain the choice of PID constants and where we surface them in the UI?

Nadia Thompson: Added flags.runtime.thermostat.disable and metric thermostat_setpoint with region tag. PID defaults are conservative; moved constants to flags and documented rationale in runbook. Will surface short form in console in a follow-up (ENG-2149).
Priya Kapoor: Concern about tenant fairness when trickle is enabled — will this starve small high-priority tenants?
Nadia Thompson: Trickler honors tenant priority weights; added unit tests for priority-preserving allocation and a fairness meter metric trickle_priority_violation (should be zero).
Liam O'Connor: CI flake on alloc_test.go — repro shows time.Sleep races. Please replace with clock mock/WaitGroup.
Nadia Thompson: Replaced test sleeps with injectible clock; pushed fix (commit b7c8d9e). CI retriggered and passed. Approved by SREs after canary telemetry review.
release_notes: Add Connection Thermostat to smooth outgoing connection ramp-ups and reduce reopen oscillation.
Introduce Slowpath Trickle-Shedder to pace slowpath admissions during overloads; reduces downstream latency spikes.
Telemetry: new metrics thermostat_setpoint, trickle_tokens_granted, trickle_priority_violation added.
Hotfix: fixes flaky alloc_test and adds canary rollback script.
